authority: Benchmark evidence hygiene only. No routing, configuration, role, capital, or execution authority follows.

budgets.max_output_tokens_justification: Largest successful observed output is 46,288 tokens (Surface A family T6). Every other family peaks at 10,603 (medians 540-3,818) against a T6 median of 25,343. 64,000 sits ~38% above that 46,288 maximum with real headroom, so the cap binds only runaway generation, never legitimate reasoning. Chosen against the observed distribution, not against any candidate's latency.
budgets.per_turn_wall_clock_s_role: Secondary stall backstop only. The token cap is the primary bound; the clock catches a genuine stall.
budgets.rationale: A token budget exists to stop a runaway, not to measure capability. Cost is out of scope, so a tight budget could only convert 'this model reasons longer' into 'this model failed' - a verbosity measurement disguised as a capability measurement, the same defect class the envelope's time-budget rationale rejects.
budgets.timeout_classification: operational_not_capability. A truncation or timeout is recorded as an operational outcome and reported separately; it is never scored as a factual failure.
budgets.tool_calls: Unchanged: 0 for every case except T4-multihop-read-recovery, which has a hard budget of 6 fixture reads. No tool-call cap is added.
budgets.why_fixed: This number never varies by candidate. A budget derived from any candidate's latency or throughput would change whenever a slower model enrolled, retroactively altering conditions for candidates already run and breaking comparability. Observed throughput varies ~2x between models (DeepSeek ~253 tok/s, GLM-flash ~130 tok/s on comparable T6 output volumes), so any latency-derived budget would partly score endpoint speed rather than reasoning.

comparability: This overlay changes dispatch conditions. Runs made before it are a different envelope and are not comparable to runs made after it. Pre-overlay runs ran under envelope.json budgets alone (600s wall-clock ceiling, provider-default token cap); post-overlay runs run under envelope.json plus this overlay (600s wall-clock backstop, 64,000 fixed output-token cap). Strict scores across that boundary must not be cited as model differentiators or merged into one board.
dispatch_conditions_changed: A fixed output-token cap of 64,000 per turn is now enforced as the primary bound.
dispatch_conditions_unchanged: 600s per-turn wall-clock ceiling (now the secondary backstop)
Strict JSON parse plus whole-object strict_equal grading (unchanged)
frozen_envelope_note: envelope.json (status frozen) is NOT edited by this overlay. Its budgets.tokens entry ('provider default; no envelope-level cap') describes pre-overlay conditions and stays as the run-of-record for pre-overlay attempts. This overlay supersedes it additively for later runs only.
known_open_question: Nobody has proven whether the two ceiling-hitting runs (empty response, null usage) would have finished given a larger budget; 'still generating' and 'looping' are externally indistinguishable from the archives alone. Separating them requires a same-model-larger-budget control run, which costs spend and is not authorized. This overlay makes that control cheap to run later by mandating truncation telemetry; it does not attempt the control.

observed_distribution.note: Established by the completed investigation; treated as given, not re-derived here.

stop_reasons.complete: A complete response was produced; grade content strictly as before.
stop_reasons.empty: No response text and no recorded cause; operational.
stop_reasons.max_output_tokens: The turn hit the 64,000 output-token cap; operational.
stop_reasons.provider_error: The provider errored before completing; operational.
stop_reasons.rule: Any stop_reason but complete is an operational outcome, reported separately, never scored as a factual failure.
stop_reasons.wall_clock: The turn hit the 600s wall-clock backstop; operational.

supersedes: Adds to the frozen envelope; modifies no frozen file, key, grader, fixture, or prompt.
